argument: Chapter 13's worked example fixes the Knight's armor at DR 4 in three places (lines 462, 488, 510), and that figure is the bestiary's outlier rather than the book's plate value. Five other chapters place plate at DR 6: ch06 fixes 6 for a plate-wearing knight on two separate lines, ch15's equipment table, ch16's armor table plus its gear walkthrough, ch17's star-metal suit (which names 6 as the plate norm while granting 7), and ch22's at-table reference sheet. Ch16's own Armor Discipline ladder puts DR 4 at breastplate and half-plate grade and reserves 6 for the three-rank plate entry, so the number in ch13 cannot stand as a deliberate downgrade of the same item; the expected value is 6 in all three citations. The same edit is owed to the bestiary Knight at line 130, and two further plate-labelled entries sit below the norm (Orc Warchief DR 3 at line 224, Death Knight DR 5 at line 627). Fix scope is mechanical and cascade-free: each of the three hits in the example totals 4 before armor, and 4 minus 4 and 4 minus 6 both collapse to the 1-damage floor, so no tier, HP ledger, or narrative beat moves. The earlier repair that re-synced the example to the bestiary carried the outlier forward, which is why ch13 now agrees with ch20 and disagrees with every chapter that defines armor; which side moves is a design call for the lead designer, but the evidence weight is five sources to one, so the armor chapters are canon and DR 4 is the propagated error.

evidence.claim: The worked example states the Knight's plate value as DR 4 at three anchors (462, 488, 510); at line 462 the Strong hit totals 4 and the subtraction bottoms out on the 1-damage floor.
The second and third citations repeat the same 4 at line 488 (Roric's warhammer) and line 510 (Kael's second round), so a repair must edit three lines, not one.

The armor chapter prices plate at DR 6 both in its table and in its purchase walkthrough; its Armor Discipline ranks place DR 4 at breastplate and half-plate grade, so a plate entry of 4 contradicts the chapter's own ladder.
A magic full-plate item states the norm explicitly when it grants one point above it, which makes 6 the stated plate baseline for the whole book.
Core resolution repeats DR 6 for plate in its damage-reduction paragraph and again in its defense example at line 150, so the norm is stated twice in the physics chapter.
The equipment table prints plate as DR 6 with a 3-Armor entry requirement, matching ch16 and ch22.
The at-table reference sheet that play groups actually use also prints plate at 6, so the quick-reference material agrees with the armor chapters.
The Knight of the Iron Circle stat block is the article ch13 matched: it labels plate at DR 4, one point below half plate's grade and two below plate's canonical value.

Two further plate-labelled stat blocks print values below the canonical 6 (Orc Warchief 3, Death Knight 5), so the plate label in the bestiary is not a reliable single value and needs a sweep, not a one-line patch.

Correcting 4 to 6 changes no output in the worked example: each of the three hits totals 4 before armor, so 4-4=0 and 4-6=-2 both floor at 1, leaving the Knight's 20-to-17 ledger, every tier call, and the narrative unchanged. Expected 4 -> 6 is a text substitution with no downstream recompute.
